correctness.rationale: For a positive finite nested tower, the superlevel sets are exactly the balls in the chain, so symmetric decreasing rearrangement recenters each layer without changing its radius. The primary fractional-gradient source gives, for every ball, the required radial-direction, nonvanishing-away-from-center-and-boundary, and integrability facts. Linearity and the pointwise Euclidean triangle inequality then give the claimed reverse endpoint inequality and the exact integrated triangle-defect identity. If the centers agree, all nonzero ball gradients are positively collinear almost everywhere. If two centers differ, then in dimension at least two the corresponding radial directions fail positive collinearity away from the affine line through the centers, while in dimension one they are opposite on the interval between the centers; in both cases strict triangle inequality holds on a positive-measure set. Thus equality is exactly the common-center case, with the one-layer case vacuous.
